newsitem.title: TURKEY: CAUSES OF TURKISH INFLATION STILL PERSIST - BANKER.
newsitem.headline: CAUSES OF TURKISH INFLATION STILL PERSIST - BANKER.

text.p: The reasons behind Turkey's chronic inflation still persist, despite an expected decline in the pace of inflation in early 1997, a senior banker said.

"A mathematical fall in (annual) inflation is very likely because high monthly inflation rates in early 1996 would be replaced by relatively lower figures this year," Burhan Karacam, general manager of Yapi Kredi Bankasi A.S., one of the leading private banks, told Reuters.
"However, the basic dynamics of the economy which create high inflation have not changed. So a higher inflation rate is expected in the second half of the year," he added.
Karacam said lira depreciation was expected to track inflation.
The downward trend in interest rates which began in late 1996 would continue in early 1997, Karacam said, but warned that interest rates might creep upward in the second half of the year.

Bond yields have plunged by some 30 percentage points since late 1996 to 80-81 percent amid rising liquidity and withholding tax raised to 12 percent from 10 percent on interest income from state securities.
Falling bond yields and expectations of lower inflation caused Turkish banks to reduce sharply their interest rates on lira deposits and loans in recent weeks.

"Falling interest rates is the most important development for the Turkish banking system in early 1997. But expectations of an uptrend in interest rates will have a stronger impact than expectations of stabilised interest rates for the rest of the year," Karacam said.

The Turkish banking sector did not face any crisis threat from short currency positions, "at least in the short-term", Karacam said, adding that falling interest rates, extended domestic borrowing maturities and the stock market's recent steep rally created an optimistic mood in the financial markets.
"The bankers' hopes are pinned on serious structural reforms to be taken on top of this optimistic environment," he added.
